items.anchor: We isolate the root inside the closed $\ell_\infty$ box
items.note: The root (c, d) is defined as the unique root of P in the closed box of radius 10^-30 around rbar (root_def, root_spec, root_unique).
The library center (a fraction with denominator 2·10^49 and 25·10^48) equals the two displayed terminating decimals exactly (norm_num on the decimal literals).

items.title: Rational root certificate
items.note: The closed box is {x : ‖x - r̄‖∞ ≤ 10^-30} (Vec 2 carries the sup norm), a root is a zero of P. "(art:seed_rho) holds" is read as: the explicit ρ = 129(c-8d)/((16c-127d-16)(127c+16d+129)) of failure.tex:92-95 satisfies 0.060 < ρ < 0.061 at every point of the box (the definition part of art:seed_rho is the failure.tex agent's item). Proved from the library: contraction of the Newton map N(h) = h - M P(r̄+h) on the box (exists_unique_root) and the coarse bounds 318/1000 < c < 319/1000, -1026/1000 < d < -1025/1000.

The library proves the lemma along this proof: rational evaluation of the Jacobian, its adjugate inverse and the eighteen Taylor coefficients (root_arithmetic), the exact expansion of the Newton map (residual_expansion, a display before M45), the contraction and self-map bounds (residual_bound, newton_lipschitz), and the interval bounds of the factors (factor_bounds).

Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M39): set on two lines (gathered). The maxima over i are bounded for every i; |ν| = ν₁+ν₂; the index set {2 ≤ |ν| ≤ 5} is certIndex.
Stated at every point of the closed box (which lies in the coarse box of the existence argument).

This proof, with the interval certificate of the subsection "Rational interval certification of all nine queries" (lines 118-157), proves Lemma art:seed_cycle (BfgsCoverage.Article.Failure.seed_cycle: the query list is Table art:trial_table for every 0 < c₁ ≤ 1/3 and c₂ > 0, the range the lemma states since the correction M11 of 15 October 2026); the certificate uses the Armijo constant 1/3 in its acceptance quantity (display 011). "the algebraic part of Lemma art:seed_cycle" (failure.tex:111-131); the other part is the interval certificate of the subsection "Rational interval certification of all nine queries" (lines 118-157, outside any proof environment, covered by its own items). Undisplayed steps stated in Lean: B(H,g,g⁺,α) = inverseBFGS H (-αHg) (g⁺-g) (update_def); the first update (SeedCycle.first_update); the middle update is C+βE (SeedCycle.middle_update gives the explicit middleMatrix); at a root β = 1/4 and γ = 1/16 (beta_gamma_root); s₀+s₁+s₂ = -(1-ρ)z₀ (displacement_closure); the matrix closure at the root (SeedCycle.source_cycle); positive curvature (g_{j+1}-g_j)ᵀs_j > 0 and positive definiteness (source_accepted_certificate, source_metric_posDef). Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M34, M38, M41, M39): the wording point noted here is resolved: the middle update is C + βE "with projected term C and rank-one term βE", and for the last update the text names the projector Π = wwᵀ onto (g₀ - g₂)^⊥, the projected term Π(C + βE)Π = ρ̃Π and the rank-one term ρ̃(I - Π), whose sum is ρ̃I (lines 93-103). Also: "The first update of the cycle, B(I,g₀,g₁,1) = M₁, is immediate from ..." (before "The first update in (art:seed_matrices)"); "For an arbitrary point (c∘,d∘), not only the root"; "clearing its nonzero denominators"; the new undisplayed step "The steps (art:seed_steps) also satisfy s_j = -α_jM_jg_j with α₀ = 1, α₁ = 1/4 and α₂ = 1/16: for j = 0, 1 by substitution, and for j = 2 by the second identity in (art:closure_identity)" (Failure.seed_matrices_steps, last conjunct); display 007 on two lines; end-of-proof mark.
β, γ, ρ̃ are the library SeedCycle.beta, gamma, rhoTilde (rfl).

items.anchor: Across one cycle, the unit-first search evaluates exactly nine trial points.
bound them by exact rational interval arithmetic
items.note: The four rules (interval_rules, mul_rule, inv_rule; before M45 a display) are sound, and induction on a rational expression proves the soundness of evaluation (enclose_sound).
An interval [a,b] (a <= b rationals) encloses a real x when a <= x <= b; the rules act on such enclosures.
The justification of display 009, stated in the same theorem: the root box lies in the first two intervals, and on them the denominator of ρ is positive and ρ lies in the third.

Corrected on 15 October 2026 with M11: the lemma now states the range 0 < c₁ ≤ 1/3, c₂ > 0, and these calculations prove it (Lean: Failure.seed_cycle): the acceptance quantity of line 143 is the Armijo test with c₁ = 1/3, so it holds for every c₁ ≤ 1/3; the positive slope gives weak Wolfe for every c₂ > 0 (positive_slope_wolfe); a rejected query fails Armijo for every c₁ > 0 (increase_rejects_armijo). seed_cycle_range_counterexample shows that the range is needed.

resolved_discrepancies.description: "Together with the matrix identities, these calculations complete the proof of Lemma art:seed_cycle" (seed_certificate.tex:199-200) asserts the lemma as printed. The printed lemma fixes no line-search constants, and its query-list claim is false for every c₁ > r₂, 0.37520 < r₂ < 0.37521 (discrepancy of A/failure/lemma/art:seed_cycle, M11; Lean: Failure.seed_cycle_range_counterexample, c₁ = 0.38, c₂ = 1/2). The calculations of this appendix prove the corrected lemma, for every 0 < c₁ ≤ 1/3 and c₂ > 0 (Lean: Failure.seed_cycle): the acceptance quantity g_jᵀz_j + αg_jᵀp_j/3 - g_iᵀq > 0 of line 181 is the Armijo test with c₁ = 1/3, hence holds for every c₁ ≤ 1/3; the positive quantity αg_iᵀp_j gives weak Wolfe for every c₂ > 0 (positive_slope_wolfe); a rejected query fails Armijo for every c₁ > 0 (increase_rejects_armijo). Same issue as the lemma; no separate correction is needed once the lemma states the range.
resolved_discrepancies.proposed: No separate change: with the range added to Lemma~\ref{art:seed_cycle} (the proposed wording of the entry for A/failure/lemma/art:seed_cycle), the sentence is correct as printed.
